description.narrative:
Progressio is a UK-based Catholic agency which specialises in providing expert development workers to work with groups which authentically represent poor and marginalised people, on a long-term basis, to help them develop lasting, practical solutions, and change the policies and structures that keep them poor.
This is the second 2-year cycle of CAFOD funding for the placement of a Progressio development worker to provide institutional capacity-building and accompaniment to CAFOD's partner Mata Dalan Institute (MDI). The first 2-year cycle began in April 2010 and ended in March 2012. MDI is a small and relatively young organisation working to increase governmental transparency and accountability, and is carrying out valuable work at the grassroots to enable communities and citizens to hold their government to account. MDI’s aim is to promote accountable public service budgeting, and improved public service delivery, through processes of budget research and analysis, empowerment and awareness-raising, participatory monitoring, and advocacy.
In this second phase, CAFOD and Progressio will continue to strengthen the organisational, programmatic, and outward communication capacity of MDI, in order to enhance citizens’ involvement in national and local decision making processes.The direct target beneficiaries are the staff of MDI (6 staff members), and their groups of volunteers in the districts, referred to as “network members” (approximately 90 individuals altogether, spread across 3 districts of East Timor). These volunteers disseminate information to communities, carry out local monitoring activities, and provide a conduit for information to be fed back up from community level. Indirect beneficiaries will be the communities themselves in the areas of operation of MDI, as the partner organisations train network members, who in turn organise communities to enable them to participate in an effective and meaningful way.
For Progressio, this current project forms part of a wider 3-year project; the Supporting Inclusive Local Governance Project, which includes supporting NGO-Forum Timor-Leste (FONGTIL), at least four District Development Networks (DDN), Core Group on Transparency (CGT), as well as Mata Dalan Institute and Fundasaun Balos (FB). Further details of this SILGP can be found in Progressio’s proposal to CAFOD, and the SILGP Concept Note, both accessible via Link Docs.
